title: Performance Optimization & Profiling ⚡
description: Use profiling tools and best practices to hit your frame‑rate targets.

slides.title: Why Optimise? ⏱️
slides.content:
# Frames Matter

Games must run smoothly: 30 FPS minimum, 60 FPS preferred. Every millisecond counts.

* **CPU** – game logic, physics, animation.
* **GPU** – rendering, materials, lights, post‑process.
* **Memory** – textures, meshes, audio.

Unreal provides powerful profiling tools to find bottlenecks.

slides.title: Performance View Modes 👀
slides.content:
## Real‑Time Heatmaps

In the editor viewport, use the **View Mode** dropdown (or Alt+ shortcuts):

* **Shader Complexity** (Alt+8) – green = fast, red = slow. Shows material cost.
* **Lighting Complexity** (Alt+7) – shows light overlap.
* **Draw Call** view – each colour is a separate draw call. Fewer = better.
* **Overdraw** – shows areas drawn multiple times (transparent objects).

Use these to quickly identify problem areas without leaving the editor.

quizData.question: Green in Shader Complexity means the material is expensive.
quizData.explanation: Green is cheap; red is expensive. Aim for mostly green in your scene.

slides.title: GPU Profiling 🎮
slides.content:
## Dive Deep

Use **ProfileGPU** in the console (press ` key then type `ProfileGPU`). It captures a frame and shows a timeline of all rendering passes.

* Look for long bars – they show heavy passes (shadows, post‑process, translucency).
* Toggle visibility of objects to see their impact.

In standalone (packaged) game, use **Unreal Insights** for deeper trace.

**Stat Commands:** `stat fps`, `stat unit`, `stat gpu` show real‑time performance overlay.

quizData.question: To see real‑time FPS and frame times, type _____ in the console.
quizData.explanation: `stat fps` and `stat unit` are essential console commands for performance monitoring.

slides.title: CPU Optimisation 🧠
slides.content:
## Game Logic Efficiency

* **Reduce Tick usage** – disable Tick on actors that don't need it (Class Defaults → Start with Tick Enabled → false).
* **Use Timers** – instead of per‑frame loops, run logic at intervals (e.g., every 0.5s).
* **Pool actors** – reuse bullets/enemies instead of spawning/destroying.
* **Avoid Casting in loops** – cache references.
* **Use LODs** (Level of Detail) – lower polycount meshes at distance.

Profilers: **Unreal Insights** records CPU/GPU/memory over time. File → Connect to session while game runs.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Texture Pool & Compression

Monitor **stat streaming** for texture memory. Reduce resolution of unseen mips, use **Texture Streaming** (enabled by default). Set **Texture LOD Bias** in materials for manual control.
